## 2026-09-29 — Prediction leagues + prediction competitions: provisional engine opus vs sonnet
Context: card "Prediction leagues with friends + multiple prediction competitions" (fullstack, P1,
short spec). Nothing like it exists: the only `PREDICT` item is the historical `series-winner`
trivia game. The card needs new models and migrations (competitions, fixtures, picks, leagues,
memberships), a new live data source for upcoming NBA games and their final scores, plus scheduled
grading, three leaderboards per competition (global, friends, league) and new UI. The spec is loose:
"a few games every week", overlapping holiday windows, "if possible several smaller tournaments".
Sonnet was defensible because a design round can break the work into explicit steps. Opus was
defensible because the risk is `high`. Registering a new app changes the settings layer, the
live schedule and results feed is a new data-pipeline source, and league invites and the friends
board read friends data.
Decision: `hard`, `risk: high`, `needsDesignRound: true`, provisional `engineModel: opus`,
`planModel: fable`. The rubric's important + complex override applies, and the loose spec means
some pieces (grading timing, overlapping competition windows, how picks lock at tip-off) need real
judgment. Design round step 5d should move the mechanical steps (CRUD views, leaderboard UI that
mirrors `Leaderboard.tsx` and `useLeaderboard`) to `[sonnet]`.
Consequences: the design round must settle the scope ("smaller tournaments" is probably a
follow-up card), where fixtures and results come from, and how grading runs. It must also name
the cost of any scheduler or feed and park if one isn't free. Friends and league boards should
follow `docs/CACHING_SCALING_PLAN.md` rather than inventing a new cache.
EOF",
  "description": "Append close-call decision entry"
}
